stories.title: Explosion hits Russian warship in Benghazi port, suspected drone attack
stories.summary: An explosion struck a Russian Steregushchiy‑class corvette docked at the Benghazi naval base at dawn on Sunday while the vessel was refuelling, and Libya’s eastern government said it was caused by a suspected drone attack. A nearby commercial ship was also hit, with minor injuries reported among its crew. Satellite and high‑resolution imagery showed a fire at the port and the corvette capsized, with only its forward bow still visible.
stories.why: The incident demonstrates the risk to foreign naval vessels operating in Libya’s eastern ports.

stories.title: Asian shares cautious as AI sell‑off worries linger, US futures rise
stories.summary: The Economic Times article reported that Asian equity markets were trading cautiously because concerns about a sell‑off in AI‑related stocks persisted. At the same time, U.S. stock futures moved higher, indicating a rebound in U.S. market sentiment. The contrasting moves highlighted mixed global risk appetite.
stories.why: Investors need to gauge the impact of AI‑sector volatility on regional portfolios and trading decisions.
stories.change: New high-signal event entered the brief.

stories.title: India and EU expected to sign free‑trade pact on Dec 16
stories.summary: An Indian official said the free‑trade agreement with the 27‑member European Union is likely to be signed on 16 December, after the two sides concluded negotiations on 27 January. The deal would grant duty‑free access for about 93 % of Indian exports to the EU and make imports of luxury cars and wines from the bloc cheaper. Together, India and the EU account for roughly 25 % of global GDP and about one‑third of world trade.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.
stories.previousTitle: India, EU likely to sign free‑trade agreement on Dec 16
stories.previousSummary: India and the 27‑member European Union are expected to sign their free‑trade agreement on 16 December, an Indian official said. Negotiations were concluded on 27 January this year, and the pact would give duty‑free access to the EU for roughly 93 % of Indian exports while lowering tariffs on luxury cars and wines from the bloc.
